task: Support role default e-mail composition preset with owner denial and Pro boundary preserved

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This permission migration has critical database authority impact. It requires negative proofs for unrelated roles, explicit individual deny, revoked membership, source identity and missing prerequisites, while only reaching a source-only assurance ceiling until real PG17 and hosted JWT acceptance.

acceptanceCriteria: The single support office.email.compose all-scope role preset is added through an idempotent new migration.
Missing catalog and role preset foundations fail before authority is changed.
Existing owner denial remains earlier than role-grant evaluation in the canonical SQL function.
No changes to existing historical migrations, other roles or hosted database.
invariants: The role-based source is the sole new authority; no new override engine is created.
The recipient author's draft remains private and server-revision protected.
Owner explicit deny takes priority over inherited support permission.
Pro Digital Office gates remain independent of permission grants.
forbiddenStates: Arbitrary compose granted to viewer or order_manager roles.
A personal allow override silently overriding explicit owner denial.
Managed migration executed before current-state baseline approval.
An unauthorized email delivery reported as verified from source tests.

failureModes: Absent permission catalog prevents valid role preset insertion.
A support preset accidentally broadens other roles through an overbroad SQL query.
Explicit owner denial loses precedence to a newly added role grant.
Adding a new SQL migration changes the 31-file package without new provenance.
edgeCases: A support employee with no personal grant gets inherited permission.
A denied support employee cannot save or send an arbitrary email.
A revoked support role no longer grants email composing.
A missing permission catalog rejects migration atomically.
Re-running SQL cannot duplicate the single support preset.

alternatives.summary: Extend the canonical role preset using a new idempotent migration scoped solely to support.
alternatives.reason: The existing explicit deny remains higher precedence and new support employees inherit email writing without management toil.

alternatives.summary: Add individual allow overrides for support staff upon account creation.
alternatives.reason: This creates unnecessary grants and risks stale permission state competing with owner denials.

alternatives.summary: Allow email writing whenever support RBAC passes without the canonical capability evaluator.
alternatives.reason: This would circumvent scoped owner denial and drift from security-definer SQL authorization.

specialistReviews.finding: A new default might accidentally defeat individual owner denial within SQL draft or queue RPCs.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep evaluate_store_capability_v1 as the only authority and verify explicit deny before role evaluation.

specialistReviews.finding: A forward SQL file might enter the immutable 31-source package without versioned source provenance.
specialistReviews.resolution: Preserve original SQL files and add this migration only after separately authorized baseline and Office dependency order.

specialistReviews.finding: A missing capability or schema table could lead to an unsafe perceived success.
specialistReviews.resolution: Make the migration reject absent foundations before the support preset insert.

specialistReviews.finding: Passing static tests cannot establish real hosted JWT and outbound sending semantics.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep source unit draft until native PostgreSQL17 and user-session acceptance evidence exist.

challenge.scenario: New support employee lacks personal allow override.
challenge.finding: The old optional capability blocked composer despite the support role.
challenge.resolution: Inherit only from canonical support permission preset.

challenge.scenario: Owner explicitly denies this capability to an active support member.
challenge.finding: A permission shortcut might incorrectly restore ability to write.
challenge.resolution: Retain denial precedence in the existing SQL evaluator.

challenge.scenario: Viewer and order manager operate in the same tenant.
challenge.finding: Broad role grants would permit unauthorized customer communications.
challenge.resolution: Insert only support with exact office.email.compose capability.

challenge.scenario: The target database lacks the original permission catalog.
challenge.finding: A partial migration would falsely claim the role is configured.
challenge.resolution: Require catalog prerequisites and fail the transaction.

challenge.scenario: The same new SQL migration runs a second time.
challenge.finding: A duplicate role grant or changed default scope could arise.
challenge.resolution: Use exact composite key conflict handling and one all scope.

challenge.scenario: An Alap account has an otherwise valid support role.
challenge.finding: A role preset might be confused with the Pro workspace entitlement.
challenge.resolution: Keep subscription plan gating untouched and separately enforced.

challenge.scenario: An email is drafted without an active approved sender mailbox.
challenge.finding: A system might falsely report delivery and lose user content.
challenge.resolution: Do not change sending mailbox gates or worker semantics.

challenge.scenario: Existing hosted Fresh Install has an empty migration ledger.
challenge.finding: Deploying out of sequence could corrupt Office migration provenance.
challenge.resolution: Do not run hosted SQL before independently approved Office baseline.

proofPlan: Run Plan Before Code with exact change base and scoped support-only migration paths.
Verify support role SQL and canonical explicit-deny precedence using targeted adversarial regressions.
Run native PostgreSQL17 integration and exact-head CI before making any successful behavior claim.
Prohibit hosted SQL until official current-state baseline and Office prerequisites are owner-approved.
operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: The existing Digital Office composer foundation introduced an optional email-compose capability without the inherited support role grant, contradicting the approved default capability and preventing support employees from writing their own customer drafts.
observableOutcomes: Authorized support members inherit office.email.compose automatically without owner extra grants.
Explicit individual denial still overrides the inherited role preset in server capability evaluation.
The Pro-only Digital Office and disabled-mailbox send boundary stay unaffected by the SQL preset correction.
unresolvedRisks: Hosted PostgreSQL and managed Supabase Auth acceptance have not been tested for this new migration.
The original Fresh Install migration adoption and 31-source forward-release blocks remain independently unresolved.
Static source assertions alone cannot certify an actual email draft save or customer delivery journey.

in: One forward-only support permission preset migration and its isolated static regression file.
Preserve historical immutable migration source and document the dependency on Office readiness.
out: No hosted database migration, baseline adoption, Auth fixtures or mailbox activation.
No admin page, customer send worker, Builder or Pro subscription policy modification.

requirements.requirement: Active support employees receive default email compose through a single inherited role preset.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No owner-denied support employee or unrelated store role gains default compose through this migration.
